bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Persistent double-digit inflation in glass, ENA, and natural gas; annual state-level pricing negotiations required (no inflation linkage); Delhi RTM reversal impacting ~4-5% of national sales; regulatory uncertainty around ethanol blending policy; potential competitive retaliation in key states.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; emphasis on resilience, premiumization, and execution; acknowledges inflation headwinds but highlights portfolio strength and operational discipline; tone optimistic on long-term margin trajectory despite near-term pressure.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 10% distribution margin on imported brands (e.g., Johnnie Walker) is benchmarked by third-party study and remains static regardless of scale — operating leverage comes from overhead absorption, not margin expansion; carton removal is primarily ESG-driven (Society 2030), not cost-driven; Smirnoff’s pocket format and on-premise activations are key to white spirits growth, not just premium whisky.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- One of the largest manufacturing networks in the Indian alcoholic beverages industry, operating 34 production facilities across the country
- Distribution ecosystem covering more than 75,000 outlets supporting wide product availability
- Diversified portfolio of 50+ owned brands plus exclusive Indian distribution/licensing of global Diageo brands (Johnnie Walker, Baileys, Smirnoff, Ciroc, Captain Morgan, etc.)
- Backing of global parent Diageo plc (majority owner via Diageo Relay B.V., ~55.88% shareholding) supporting brand equity, category expertise and international scale
- Portfolio-led, premiumisation-anchored strategy — Prestige & Above segment contributes 89.6% of net sales value and grew net sales 8.6% in FY2025-26
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Fragmented, state-by-state regulatory framework — India's alcobev industry is highly decentralised, with state governments controlling licensing, taxation, legal drinking age and retail distribution; compliance requirements, fees and procedures differ across regions, creating operational challenges and higher costs for a pan-India operator like USL.
- Maharashtra Made Liquor (MML) policy distortion — Maharashtra's August 2025 low-tax MML category, eligibility for which is linked to local manufacturing/ownership, limits participation by national players like USL that manufacture outside the state, creating a significant price/competitive distortion, narrowing consumer choice and complicating production and supply-chain planning.
- High and rising taxation on alcoholic beverages — Multiple layers of excise duties, VAT and state surcharges are a major component of the sector's regulatory landscape, contributing to relatively high retail prices that can constrain consumption growth, particularly for price-sensitive segments.
- Frequent, unpredictable state-level regulatory change — Every year several states revise their regulatory framework for alcoholic beverages (e.g. Karnataka's April 2026 excise overhaul, Maharashtra's MML framework), adding planning uncertainty even where reforms are ultimately favourable.
- Cybersecurity risk — The Risk Management Committee's terms of reference explicitly include evaluating and ensuring appropriate processes and systems to monitor and report cyber security risks, indicating this is a Board-level watch item.
- Geopolitical and macroeconomic risk — The Risk Management Committee reviewed geopolitical and macroeconomic factors during the year as risks that could impact the Company's strategy, operations and stakeholders.
- Business continuity risk — The Risk Management Committee reviewed business continuity risk during the year as part of its enterprise risk oversight, alongside regulatory/policy developments and cyber security.

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin at 39.5% (-720-730 bps vs normalized due to double-digit input inflation); EBITDA margin at 15.5%; cost discipline on overheads offsetting 1/3 of inflation; carton removal (sustainability-driven) to reduce packaging costs from Q1FY24.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Mid-to-high teens EBITDA margin target maintained; expects pricing to ramp up in Q3/FY23, but gross margin under pressure from double-digit input inflation (glass, ENA, natural gas); A&P spend to gradually increase from 5.5% to 8-9% of net sales.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion of craft gin (Hapusa, Greater Than) and white spirits; potential entry into ready-to-drink (RTD) category if consumer traction accelerates; international rollout of Godawan (UK, US); e-commerce DTC expansion in West Bengal via Swiggy, Boozy, Bigbasket.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Portfolio-led growth strategy anchored in premiumisation, core brand renovation, innovation and consumer-centricity
- Advancing analytics and AI to scale machine learning and predictive/prescriptive capabilities for demand forecasting, supply planning and commercial decisions
- Deepening consumer engagement through richer consumer data platforms, real-time feedback loops and more personalised marketing interventions
- Strengthening commercial technology by integrating sales, market, finance and execution data for deeper channel visibility
- Building a smarter digital core via a planned S/4HANA transformation, with greater use of AI, robotics and workflow orchestration
- Driving supply excellence through AI/IoT-enabled demand sensing, digital procurement, sensor-based monitoring and distillery analytics
- Strategic investments in high-growth adjacencies outside core spirits (Nao Spirits gin brands, V9 Beverages non-alcoholic alternatives)
- Disciplined capital allocation and portfolio optimisation, including proposed divestment of non-core investments (RCSPL)
- People strategy pillars — Advantaged Capabilities, Talent Sustainability, Thriving Organisation, and Inclusion & Diversity — to build a future-ready organisation
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: USL's growth is being driven primarily by portfolio premiumisation rather than disclosed new plant capacity additions: the Prestige & Above (P&A) segment delivered net sales value of Rs.11,152 crore (up 8.6%), supported by growth in luxury and Bottled-in-Origin/Bottled-in-India brands, scaling of Indian single malt Godawan and tequila Don Julio, Smirnoff flavour innovation (e.g. Minty Jamun) and expansion of Pocket Pack formats for accessibility and penetration. The Company continues to run a multi-year supply agility programme to optimise its manufacturing footprint, logistics efficiency and inventory management, and anticipates potential medium-term cost relief on bulk Scotch inputs upon implementation of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement. Separately, the Company has stated longer-term sustainability targets (net zero across Scopes 1, 2 and 3 by 2050; 100% recyclable/reusable/compostable packaging; recycled content in packaging raised to 50% by 2030 and in plastic bottles to 35% by 2025 with sequential improvement to 2030; zero waste to landfill in direct operations; regenerative agriculture programmes implemented by 2030).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's GDP grew 7.7% in FY2025-26 versus 7.1% the prior year, with resilient domestic consumption providing a favourable backdrop for discretionary and premium consumption categories
- Favourable demographics — a rising number of young adults entering the legal drinking age, coupled with increasing disposable incomes, expected to boost demand particularly in premium and aspirational segments
- Premiumisation — rising affluence and aspiration accelerating the shift towards premium and super-premium alcoholic beverages, seen as accretive to margins
- Emergence of craft and niche segments (craft spirits, flavoured products, RTDs) expanding consumption occasions and attracting new consumers
- Growth of modern/organised retail and digital engagement improving product accessibility and brand visibility
- India-UK Free Trade Agreement expected to reduce import duties on Scotch whisky and gin from 150% to 75% (phased to 40% over the next decade), expected to accelerate premiumisation and improve Scotch accessibility
- Karnataka's April 2026 excise reform (Alcohol-in-Beverage taxation, removal of retail price controls, excise slabs cut from 16 to 8) seen as a structural simplification that could expedite premiumisation in the state
- Regulatory fragmentation remains a constraint — Maharashtra's new low-tax Maharashtra Made Liquor category (August 2025) creates market distortion and competitive complexity for national players operating outside the state
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: United Spirits Limited is accelerating premiumization through portfolio reshaping, innovation in craft and white spirits, and operational efficiency, driving strong top-line growth despite inflationary headwinds in glass and ENA. The divestment of popular segment brands has unlocked capital and sharpened focus on high-margin prestige categories, positioning USL for sustained EBITDA resilience and margin expansion in the medium term.

open.item: Board recommended a final dividend of Rs.11 per equity share for FY2025-26 (record date 8 July 2026, payable on/after 13 August 2026), taking the total FY2025-26 dividend to Rs.17 per share at a 68% payout ratio, in line with the updated dividend distribution policy.

USL launched a comprehensive renovation of McDowell's No. 1 (re-engineered liquid with 30% more Scotch, new pack design, new aspirational 180ml PET format) in Uttar Pradesh, to be rolled out pan-India through FY 2026-27.

USL is divesting its 100% stake in Royal Challengers Sports Pvt Ltd (owner of the Royal Challengers Bengaluru IPL/WPL franchise) for approximately Rs.16,663 crore; RCSPL has been classified as discontinued operations pending approval from the Board of Control for Cricket in India, the Competition Commission of India and other regulatory authorities.

The Board approved the sale of 14,690 equity shares of Royal Challengers Sports Pvt Ltd (RCSPL) for an aggregate consideration of Rs.16,663 crore, subject to conditions in the Share Purchase Agreement dated 24 March 2026 (as amended and restated on 11 May 2026 following a purchaser change).
USL holds 97.07% of NAO Spirits & Beverages Private Limited and has an obligation to buy the remaining equity interest from the third-party shareholder upon receipt of certain regulatory approvals.

USL plans an S/4HANA transformation to create a stronger, more standardised digital backbone, alongside greater use of AI, robotics and workflow orchestration for end-to-end automation across functions.
USL plans to roll out Transport Management System (TMS) 2.0 and digital order management platforms to enhance logistics efficiency, traceability and end-to-end visibility.
USL (Diageo India) targets net zero across Scopes 1, 2 and 3 by 2050.
USL targets ensuring 100% of its packaging is recyclable (or reusable/compostable).
USL targets increasing the percentage of recycled content in its packaging to 50% by 2030.
USL targets increasing average recycled content in its plastic bottles to 35% by 2025, with sequential improvement through 2030 subject to quality and availability.
USL targets achieving zero waste created intended for landfill in its direct operations.

USL targets implementing regenerative agriculture programmes by 2030, and providing agricultural skills and resources to strengthen resilience and economic prosperity of smallholder farmers in its key ingredient sourcing landscapes.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Premium & Luxury: 23% P&A growth; Royal Challenge (renovated): strong growth in Maharashtra, Telangana, Delhi; McDowell’s No.1: resilient despite lower prestige segment headwinds; Godawan (Indian single malt): now in 5 states + UAE, launching in UK/US; Gin & Vodka: double-digit growth (Tanqueray, Gordon’s, Smirnoff); Popular segment: fully divested (32 brands sold, 11 franchised).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Owned brand portfolio (P&A / Popular / Other segments):** Godawan, McDowell's No. 1, Royal Challenge, Signature, Antiquity, Black Dog, Director's Special Black, McDowell's Rum, McDowell's Brandy, McDowell's X-Series
- **International brands distributed under license:** Don Julio, Singleton, Tanqueray, Captain Morgan, Johnnie Walker, J&B, Baileys, Lagavulin, Talisker, VAT 69, Black & White, Smirnoff, Ciroc

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India — pan-India retail distribution (>75,000 outlets)
- On-premise channel: bars, restaurants, hotels and nightlife venues

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Mid-to-high teens EBITDA margin target maintained; expects pricing to ramp up in Q3/FY23, but gross margin under pressure from double-digit input inflation (glass, ENA, natural gas); A&P spend to gradually increase from 5.5% to 8-9% of net sales.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion of craft gin (Hapusa, Greater Than) and white spirits; potential entry into ready-to-drink (RTD) category if consumer traction accelerates; international rollout of Godawan (UK, US); e-commerce DTC expansion in West Bengal via Swiggy, Boozy, Bigbasket.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's GDP grew 7.7% in FY2025-26 versus 7.1% the prior year, with resilient domestic consumption providing a favourable backdrop for discretionary and premium consumption categories
- Favourable demographics — a rising number of young adults entering the legal drinking age, coupled with increasing disposable incomes, expected to boost demand particularly in premium and aspirational segments
- Premiumisation — rising affluence and aspiration accelerating the shift towards premium and super-premium alcoholic beverages, seen as accretive to margins
- Emergence of craft and niche segments (craft spirits, flavoured products, RTDs) expanding consumption occasions and attracting new consumers
- Growth of modern/organised retail and digital engagement improving product accessibility and brand visibility
- India-UK Free Trade Agreement expected to reduce import duties on Scotch whisky and gin from 150% to 75% (phased to 40% over the next decade), expected to accelerate premiumisation and improve Scotch accessibility
- Karnataka's April 2026 excise reform (Alcohol-in-Beverage taxation, removal of retail price controls, excise slabs cut from 16 to 8) seen as a structural simplification that could expedite premiumisation in the state
- Regulatory fragmentation remains a constraint — Maharashtra's new low-tax Maharashtra Made Liquor category (August 2025) creates market distortion and competitive complexity for national players operating outside the state

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin at 39.5% (-720-730 bps vs normalized due to double-digit input inflation); EBITDA margin at 15.5%; cost discipline on overheads offsetting 1/3 of inflation; carton removal (sustainability-driven) to reduce packaging costs from Q1FY24.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: INR 420cr working capital released from divestment (INR 285cr from slump sale, INR 140cr from franchising); focus on reinvesting in premium portfolio, A&P, and innovation; no dividend or buyback guidance mentioned; surplus cash to be deployed in growth initiatives.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: USL's growth is being driven primarily by portfolio premiumisation rather than disclosed new plant capacity additions: the Prestige & Above (P&A) segment delivered net sales value of Rs.11,152 crore (up 8.6%), supported by growth in luxury and Bottled-in-Origin/Bottled-in-India brands, scaling of Indian single malt Godawan and tequila Don Julio, Smirnoff flavour innovation (e.g. Minty Jamun) and expansion of Pocket Pack formats for accessibility and penetration. The Company continues to run a multi-year supply agility programme to optimise its manufacturing footprint, logistics efficiency and inventory management, and anticipates potential medium-term cost relief on bulk Scotch inputs upon implementation of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement. Separately, the Company has stated longer-term sustainability targets (net zero across Scopes 1, 2 and 3 by 2050; 100% recyclable/reusable/compostable packaging; recycled content in packaging raised to 50% by 2030 and in plastic bottles to 35% by 2025 with sequential improvement to 2030; zero waste to landfill in direct operations; regenerative agriculture programmes implemented by 2030).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and strategic; emphasis on resilience, premiumization, and execution; acknowledges inflation headwinds but highlights portfolio strength and operational discipline; tone optimistic on long-term margin trajectory despite near-term pressure.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the largest manufacturing networks in the Indian alcoholic beverages industry, operating 34 production facilities across the country
- Distribution ecosystem covering more than 75,000 outlets supporting wide product availability
- Diversified portfolio of 50+ owned brands plus exclusive Indian distribution/licensing of global Diageo brands (Johnnie Walker, Baileys, Smirnoff, Ciroc, Captain Morgan, etc.)
- Backing of global parent Diageo plc (majority owner via Diageo Relay B.V., ~55.88% shareholding) supporting brand equity, category expertise and international scale
- Portfolio-led, premiumisation-anchored strategy — Prestige & Above segment contributes 89.6% of net sales value and grew net sales 8.6% in FY2025-26

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Persistent double-digit inflation in glass, ENA, and natural gas; annual state-level pricing negotiations required (no inflation linkage); Delhi RTM reversal impacting ~4-5% of national sales; regulatory uncertainty around ethanol blending policy; potential competitive retaliation in key states.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 10% distribution margin on imported brands (e.g., Johnnie Walker) is benchmarked by third-party study and remains static regardless of scale — operating leverage comes from overhead absorption, not margin expansion; carton removal is primarily ESG-driven (Society 2030), not cost-driven; Smirnoff’s pocket format and on-premise activations are key to white spirits growth, not just premium whisky.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Portfolio-led growth strategy anchored in premiumisation, core brand renovation, innovation and consumer-centricity
- Advancing analytics and AI to scale machine learning and predictive/prescriptive capabilities for demand forecasting, supply planning and commercial decisions
- Deepening consumer engagement through richer consumer data platforms, real-time feedback loops and more personalised marketing interventions
- Strengthening commercial technology by integrating sales, market, finance and execution data for deeper channel visibility
- Building a smarter digital core via a planned S/4HANA …

themes.need: Alco-bev players ride premium-&-above mix shift, single-malt/gin launches and state-excise/route-to-market dynamics - a pricing-power thesis distinct from staple rural-recovery/GST pull.
themes.driver: Premium-mix up-trading, single-malt/gin launches and state-excise/route-to-market dynamics.

hero.oneLiner: Diageo India (United Spirits Limited) is one of India's leading beverage alcohol manufacturers, majority-owned by Diageo plc, with a premium and diversified portfolio spanning Prestige & Above and Popular segments.

developments.text: completes its July investment in Nuvola Spirits, **taking 17,350 compulsorily convertible preference shares and 10 equity shares for Rs 2.69 crore**, 10.08% of the company on a fully diluted basis.
